correctness.rationale: Three mutually exclusive hub-occupancy cases exhaust every vertex subset. Singleton-page forced partners and matching parity give the two-hub polynomial terms; unique-hub case forces all same-side page vertices and exactly one omitted opposite vertex; hub-free case forces every full page. Strict-subset comparison, not merely single deletion, proves the minimal-family statement. Independent exhaustive original-definition verifier confirms family equality, coefficients, and minimality for r=2..8 (349,504 candidate subsets). Universal scope follows from proof, not enumeration.

value.rationale: For a natural planar, bipartite, two-vertex-connected graph-product family, the result resolves the entire paired-dominating vertex-set distribution and all inclusion-minimal sets. Its striking contrast—every feasible even set size occurs, but r−2 intermediate even sizes never occur minimally—gives an unbounded gap across an infinite family, beyond merely computing a minimum or maximum parameter.
